title: What the predicted-map study found
scope: Aggregate author analysis of AlphaGenome-predicted GM12878 contact maps. These are reported research results, separate from the synthetic browser presets. Clinical-credit comparisons in replication are descriptive.
findings: All 360 discovery and 252 replication comparisons numerically saturated the specified endpoint bound.
Centering resolved 72 and 66 native ties while preserving all 45 and 18 strict native leaders.
Selected-allele credit rose slightly in discovery and decreased descriptively in replication; sharper ranks did not establish a consistent clinical-credit gain.
Native-diagram witness bounds identified 44 and 34 additional unique endpoint leaders beyond the simple margin bounds. No runtime speedup was benchmarked.
No discovery main or sensitivity test survived Holm adjustment over all sixteen tests. No new confirmatory clinical-enrichment test was added in replication.
limits: Predicted maps on one GM12878 track, not matched experimental Hi-C measurements.
Selected sites and overlapping within-gene windows limit generalization.
Prospective status concerns new spatial outcomes; model-training independence and immutable server weights were not established.
Practical numerical allowances are not a complete validated-arithmetic certificate.
Higher-precision source outputs would be needed to isolate the causal contribution of quantization.
